notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 7th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Rasmus Ristolainen is out and has missed the last 6 games. Jamie Drysdale has taken his spot beside Travis Sanheim. That pair has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 88:13 together, up from 23% with Ristolainen.
Nikita Grebenkin is out at least four months (back surgery) and has not played this season. Sean Couturier has taken his spot beside Owen Tippett and Trevor Zegras.
David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 43% of the team’s power-play time in 9 games, up from 2% last season.

story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Canucks are on a five-game losing streak, and the Flyers are winless in three (0-2-1). Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Flyers are last in the Metropolitan (29th in the NHL) and the Canucks are last in the NHL.

The Flyers haven’t played well, but their record (.342) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .394, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Canucks (.184 on chances worth .329), where their goaltending has held them back.

The Canucks (lowest) and the Flyers (3rd lowest) both pick their shots. The Flyers get a lot of their shots blocked (30th). Philadelphia has scored 2.21 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. On the other side, the Canucks have had shaky goaltending (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (32nd). Vancouver has allowed 4.58 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Flyers (2nd lowest), so expect a tight one.

Trevor Zegras (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 19 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Matvei Michkov (10 G / 3 A / 13 P in 19 GP) has a team-high ten goals. For the Canucks, Elias Pettersson (#40) (4 G / 15 A / 19 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Brock Boeser (7 G / 9 A / 16 P in 19 GP) has a team-high seven goals.
Joseph Woll (1-6-2 / .898 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to start for Philadelphia, and Leevi Meriläinen (2-7-1 / .889 SV% in 11 GS) for Vancouver.
